name: CM Spine (Zeng et al., Electronics 2024): 208 intraoperative lumbar G-arm images
what: 208 anteroposterior lumbar spine images at 1024 x 1024, taken during surgery with a mobile dual-mode G-arm (Geelin500-A), of patients with lumbar disc herniation or vertebral compression fractures, each lumbar vertebra in view annotated by its level, L1 to L5, 537 vertebrae, split 148 and 60 in the paper (Zeng et al., Electronics 2024;13(11):2137); the paper's data statement points to its repository, github.com/zengyuyuyu/Neighbor, whose README linked this Drive file as the set and whose code reads the set as COCO files (train2022, val2022, spine_train.json, spine_val.json); on 2026-10-23 the repository is no longer public and the Drive file does not open, so the set is held by its authors alone
level_truth: each lumbar vertebra's level, L1 to L5, as the authors annotated it
licence: none stated: the paper's data statement and its repository's README name no licence, and the repository has no licence file (read 2026-10-23)
how_to_get: Open https://drive.google.com/file/d/1r9wX1802gkU4-EQHMMlyAlEiWXGWLhhJ/view logged in to the owner's Google account: a page saying you need access offers Request access, one press that mails the file's owner; a page saying the file does not exist means it is gone (the Drive API answers not found for both, 2026-10-23).

Send letters/cm_spine_drive_file.md from the owner's mailbox to the corresponding authors, Erkang Cheng (ekcheng@iim.ac.cn) and Bo Song (songbo@iim.ac.cn), with the first author Yu Zeng (yzeng@iim.ac.cn) in copy; the addresses are the paper's own.

If no answer comes in two weeks, write to the journal's editorial office (electronics@mdpi.com, or the ethics team at publication.ethics@mdpi.com) citing the paper's Data Availability Statement, which names the repository as where code and data are; MDPI's ethics page asks authors who remove data to tell the office, and asks a reader to write to the corresponding author first.

Once a copy is offered, the fetch is a Slurm job on the owner's word, never on the login node; the data platform's route (python3 data/reproduce/reacquire/reacquire.py --grid cm_spine_drive_file) works only if the Drive file comes back.
